description: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine-shaped warmdown in get_lr_multiplier.
Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate anneals over most of the run.
Only sync the loss with .item() (and do NaN check and logging) every 20 steps instead of every step.
Set HEAD_DIM to 64 so the model uses 8 attention heads of dim 64 instead of 4 heads of dim 128. FA3 supports head dim 64, and the dim stays 512.
Set DEPTH to 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads of dim 128, already divisible) so the smaller model sees more tokens in 300s.

issues: The diff changes one hyperparameter, DEPTH from 8 to 6. It does not touch the evaluation call, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import line or the final summary printing. No integrity problem found.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. A shallower model takes more optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, so a lower val_bpb is plausible. Check that the model dimension derived from DEPTH is still valid, for example divisible by the head dimension. The harness gave valid results for both runs, which suggests it is.

I can't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's standard deviation or standard error was not provided. Candidate mean = (1.0829 + 1.0825) / 2 = 1.0827. The difference from the incumbent mean of 1.1145 is 0.0318. For z = 7.749, the standard error would have to be about 0.0041. That is consistent with the spread of the candidate runs and typical run-to-run noise, so the reported z looks plausible.
There are only 2 candidate runs, but the effect is large (about 0.032 bpb) and the two runs agree closely (0.0004 apart). The accept decision is reasonable.
Simplicity: the change shrinks the model and adds no code, which counts in its favor.

description: Set DEPTH to 6 (model_dim 384, 3 heads of dim 128, already divisible) so the smaller model sees more tokens in 300s.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.3 so more of the time budget is spent at full learning rate.

issues: No integrity issue: the diff changes one modelling line. It multiplies q and k by 1.2 after the QK norm, which scales the attention logits by 1.44. It does not touch the metric, the data, the seed lines, the prepare.py import or the evaluation call.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The change is valid and works with flash_attn_func's default softmax scale. Its effect could also be gained by tuning the softmax scale or a learnable QK gain, so it is a hyperparameter tweak rather than a new mechanism.

I can't recompute z exactly. Only one candidate run (1.0806) and the incumbent mean (1.0827 over 2 runs) were given, without per-run values or a noise SD. The gap of 0.0021 and the reported z of 0.318 imply a noise SD of about 0.0066, which I can't check from these numbers.

The numbers match the decision. One candidate run is not enough evidence, and z = 0.318 is well below any usual threshold, so 'reject' is consistent. The gap is in the right direction but is within noise. A replicate run would be needed before accepting it.

description: Scale q and k by a fixed 1.2 after RMS norm (attention logits x1.44) to sharpen attention; fixed rather than learnable since 1-D params in blocks would break the Muon grouping.
Replace the ReLU^2 MLP with a SwiGLU-style gated SiLU MLP, hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64, to keep the parameter count about the same.
No change: attention and MLP output projections are already zero-initialised in init_weights.
Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 once after gradient accumulation, just before the optimizer step.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (grad accumulation 4 -> 2 at device batch 64) so the small model takes more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.

issues: No integrity problem found. The diff changes one hyperparameter: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE goes from 2**19 to 2**18. It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call or the summary printing.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. With DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and a sequence length of 2048, 2**18 is still a whole multiple of the tokens per micro-batch (gradient accumulation goes from 4 steps to 2). Halving the batch also gives about twice as many optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s, which plausibly explains the gain.
The learning rates were not rescaled for the smaller batch. That is a tuning question, not an integrity problem.

The numbers support the claim. The candidate mean is 1.06535 against an incumbent mean of 1.0827, a gain of about 0.0174 bpb. The two candidate runs are within 0.0003 of each other. The reported z = 3.165 is consistent with accepting.

I can't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's per-run values and variance aren't provided. From the numbers given, z = 3.165 implies a pooled standard error of about 0.0055. With only n=2 on each side, that estimate is rough.

description: Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (grad accumulation 4 -> 2 at device batch 64) so the small model takes more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Set ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) so Adam's second-moment estimate is smoother.
Change Muon momentum schedule to ramp 0.85->0.97 over 300 steps, hold 0.97 until warmdown, then linearly decay to 0.9 during warmdown.

issues: No integrity problem. The diff changes only has_ve() so every layer gets a Value Embedding, not alternating layers. This is an architecture change. It leaves val_bpb measurement, the data, the seed lines and the evaluation call alone.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. has_ve() is the single place that decides which layers get value embeddings, so returning True applies the change the same way wherever it is called. One side effect: it adds parameters and VRAM for the extra value-embedding tables and gates. That is allowed, since VRAM is a soft constraint and the training time is fixed.

The numbers are consistent. The candidate scored 1.0604 against an incumbent mean of 1.0654, a difference of 0.0050. A z of 0.740 implies a pooled noise scale of about 0.0068. That is plausible for 1 candidate run against 2 incumbent runs, but I can't check it exactly because the per-run incumbent values and the standard deviation were not given.
With only one candidate run and z = 0.74, the gain is not separated from noise, so 'reject' as the provisional decision is reasonable. If a slot is spent on it, a replicate run would settle it.

The change is very small and reads as an improvement, but it also removes the alternating logic and leaves has_ve() as a trivial function. If this is adopted, simplify it: remove the dead parameters or inline the check.

description: Put value embeddings on every layer instead of alternating layers by making has_ve always return True.
Set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.1 for Muon cautious weight decay.
Set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the learning rate keeps a small nonzero value at the end of warmdown.
Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSSL" so with DEPTH 6 five layers use half-context sliding window and the final layer stays full attention.
Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 to test whether the Muon optimum moved after the smaller model and batch.
Change initial per-layer scalars in init_weights: resid_lambdas 1.0 -> 0.9 and x0_lambdas 0.1 -> 0.2.
